title: Burp Recon — WSTG-INFO/CONF: Map the Full Attack Surface
body: WSTG-INFO (10 tests) and WSTG-CONF (12 tests). You cannot test what you haven't found. Every endpoint, parameter, technology, and configuration weakness discovered here feeds the other categories. Passive recon happens automatically as you browse — active discovery with Spider, Param Miner, and feroxbuster fills the gaps. The technology fingerprint tells you the parameter naming convention before you touch a single input.
cmd:
# ══ ⭐ RECON ORDER — map before you test ══════════════════════════════

# 0) PASSIVE FINGERPRINT — from the initial scan response headers
# In HTTP History, pick any response -> check headers:
#   Server: Apache/2.4.38           -> Apache version, check for CVEs
#   X-Powered-By: PHP/7.4           -> PHP version, check for type juggling, CVEs
#   Set-Cookie: _boolean_session    -> Ruby on Rails (Rack session + authenticity_token)
#   Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID           -> PHP session
#   Set-Cookie: JSESSIONID          -> Java/Tomcat -> try .jsp/.jspx webshells
#   Set-Cookie: laravel_session     -> Laravel PHP
#   X-AspNet-Version                -> ASP.NET -> try .aspx shells
#   X-Generator: WordPress          -> WordPress -> web_enum -> wordpress node
#   ETag/Date headers               -> can leak server time (token prediction)
# Framework identifies parameter syntax:
#   Rails + Laravel  -> user[field]=value (bracket syntax, see burp_authn)
#   Spring/flat JSON -> field=value or {"field":"value"}
#   GraphQL          -> {"query":"..."} body, introspection at /graphql

# 1) BROWSER WALK — passive map
# Browse the entire app normally with Burp proxy on and scope set.
# Target -> Site map builds automatically from traffic.
# Click every link, submit every form, trigger every function.
# After: Target -> Site map -> filter by response code
#   200 = live endpoints     302 = redirects (follow them, check Location:)
#   403 = exists but locked  (retry w/ trailing slash, different verb, see CONF)
#   500 = error (server-side exception — check error body for paths/stack traces)

# 2) SPIDER / CRAWL (WSTG-INFO-06)
# Target -> right-click host -> Spider this host (Community)
# Pro: Target -> right-click -> Scan -> Crawl only (deeper, handles JS-heavy apps)
# After spider: Target -> Site map -> Show only in-scope items
# Engagement Tools -> Find comments  (extracts HTML comments from all responses)
# Engagement Tools -> Find scripts   (extracts all JS endpoints and parameters)

# 3) JS FILE ANALYSIS — where parameters and API endpoints hide
# Target -> Site map -> filter for Content-Type: javascript (or .js extension)
# For each JS file: Engagement Tools -> Find scripts (extracts fetch/xhr/axios URLs)
# Or: open JS in browser DevTools -> Ctrl+F for:
#   fetch(   xhr.open(   axios.get(   $.ajax(   api/   /v1/   /v2/
#   endpoint   userId   confirmed   role   token   secret   key   password
# JS source often reveals:
#   API base URLs and versioned endpoints (/api/v2/users/{id})
#   Parameter names (userId, confirmed, role, validated, debug)
#   Auth flow logic (how tokens are stored, refreshed, validated)
#   Hardcoded API keys or secrets (search for: apiKey, secret, token =)
# Tool: Linkfinder (automates JS endpoint extraction)
python3 linkfinder.py -i http://$ip/assets/app.js -o cli

# 4) CONTENT DISCOVERY — feroxbuster / ffuf (WSTG-INFO-04)
feroxbuster -u http://$ip -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/raft-medium-directories.txt   -x php,txt,bak,zip,conf,config,xml,json -d 2 -C 404,503   --dont-scan 'assets,img,css,js,vendor,fonts'   --filter-similar-to http://$ip/doesnotexist123
# Parse output (sort -uf folds case-duplicates — Assets/ASSETS/assets -> one line):
grep -iE '\.(php|aspx?|jsp|cgi)' ferox.txt | grep -vE '^(404|403)' | awk '{print $NF}' | sort -uf
grep -E '^(401|403)' ferox.txt | awk '{print $NF}' | sort -uf   # retry w/ trailing slash
grep -iE 'upload|admin|backup|config|api|dev' ferox.txt | awk '{print $NF}' | sort -uf

# 5) PARAM MINER — find hidden parameters (WSTG-INFO-*)
# HTTP History -> right-click any interesting request -> Extensions -> Param Miner
# Options: Guess GET params / Guess POST params / Guess headers / Guess everything
# Output: Extensions -> Param Miner -> Output tab
# How it works: sends request with a candidate param -> compares response to baseline
#   Any response difference (even 1 byte) = that parameter is processed by the server
# Finds: debug=true, admin=1, validated=true, test=1, internal=true, cache=false

# 6) WSTG-CONF — configuration checks
# HTTP Methods: OPTIONS, PUT, DELETE, TRACE, PATCH allowed?
curl -X OPTIONS http://$ip/ -v 2>&1 | grep -i "allow:"
#   TRACE enabled -> XST (cross-site tracing) attack surface
#   PUT on a directory -> direct file upload without auth
#   DELETE -> may allow removing files or resources
# Common sensitive paths (always check):
curl -s http://$ip/robots.txt       # Disallow: often shows hidden paths
curl -s http://$ip/sitemap.xml      # complete URL list
curl -s http://$ip/.git/HEAD        # git repo exposed -> git dumper
curl -s http://$ip/.env             # Laravel/Node env file (DB creds, API keys)
curl -s http://$ip/wp-config.php    # WordPress config (DB creds)
curl -s http://$ip/config.php       # generic PHP config
curl -s http://$ip/web.config       # IIS config (may expose connection strings)
curl -s http://$ip/phpinfo.php      # phpinfo() -> full server config disclosure
curl -s http://$ip/server-status    # Apache mod_status (active requests + IPs)
curl -s http://$ip/server-info      # Apache mod_info (config + modules)
# Admin panels at common paths:
# /admin /administrator /manage /dashboard /panel /console /cpanel /phpmyadmin
# /manager (Tomcat) /jenkins /grafana /nagios /zabbix /kibana
# Default creds if panel found: admin:admin admin:password admin:admin123
#   app-specific: tomcat:s3cret jenkins:jenkins pi:raspberry root:root

# 7) SECURITY HEADERS AUDIT (WSTG-CONF-07)
curl -si http://$ip/ | grep -iE "x-frame-options|content-security-policy|x-xss-protection|strict-transport|x-content-type|referrer-policy|permissions-policy"
# Missing X-Frame-Options    -> clickjacking possible
# Missing CSP                -> XSS impact amplified (no script-src restriction)
# Missing X-Content-Type     -> MIME sniffing -> XSS via uploaded files
# Missing HSTS               -> SSL stripping possible over HTTP
warn: JS analysis is where the real surface lives in modern apps — API endpoints, parameter names, and auth token handling are all there. Do it before testing anything else. Tech fingerprinting from response headers tells you the parameter naming convention (Rails authenticity_token = user[field] syntax) before you touch a single input. Never skip robots.txt, .git, and .env — they're the highest-yield two-second checks in reconnaissance.
